title.en: Field query Geometric nearest sample on any matching planar arrays

summary: Choose flattened point of minimum squared coordinate distance

capability: Choose the flattened sample with minimum squared coordinate distance to each query point.
operation: matched planar sample arrays, field values and query points -> sampled field values
discovery.model: Geometric nearest-neighbor selection in matched planar coordinates; no interpolation.
discovery.geometry: Planar matched sample points with x column and y row coordinates, or matched scattered arrays; queries are ordered coordinate pairs.
discovery.boundary: No out-of-support interpolation is synthesized; finite matched samples and queries inside the convex/interpolation support are required, and equivalence with the rectangular scheme on irregular grids is not asserted.

inputs.name: X
inputs.constraints: For rectangular nearest X[0,:] is x axis

inputs.name: Y

preconditions: Finite matched planar sample arrays and fields
Requested grid/query points lie inside convex/interpolation support
supported: Finite inputs satisfying the callable-specific shape, support, and boundary conditions
excluded: Rectangular and geometric nearest schemes are not asserted equivalent on irregular input
Outside-support and nonfinite-field cases are unqualified

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError or the underlying NumPy/SciPy exception for nonfinite, mismatched, unsorted, out-of-domain, or malformed inputs; no input repair is inferred.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Numerical, interpolation, or optional-dependency exceptions propagate from the direct calculation.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; the relation uses direct finite-difference, interpolation, selection, or quadrature operations.
failure_semantics.partial_results: No partial result is promised when input validation or the underlying numerical operation fails.

example.description: Query the value at the geometrically nearest point in a matched planar sample.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.geometry.sampling import locs_to_vals1D

x, y = np.meshgrid([0.0, 0.5, 1.0], [0.0, 0.5, 1.0])
values = locs_to_vals1D(x, y, x + 2.0 * y, [(0.5, 0.5)])
np.testing.assert_allclose(values, [1.5])
